text:
Questioned the need of the Airport Spur in light of the reconstruction of Grange Avenue and College Avenue.
Stated that noise can interfere with normal activities and cause psychological problems for people.
Questioned why average school hour traffic was used instead of peak school hour traffic at Hamlin-Garland School.
The Draft EIS ignored the fact that approximately 40 residents adjacent to the Airport Spur will experience noise levels above the federal standards.
He questioned why an 8% truck mix was used for the Airport Spur while existing I-94 has a 15% truck mix.
See the response to Witness 11 on page 236.
See pages 139 and 150 for a response.
The regular school hours at Hamlin-Garland School are from 9:00 A.M. to 3:00 P.M. and this does not correspond to the normal existing or future projected peak weekday traffic hours of 7:00-9:00 A.M. and 3:00-6:00 P.M. The use of the average daytime traffic rather than peak traffic is permitted by federal standards for calculating noise levels at schools and represents a more normal condition.
See pages 139 and 140 for a response.
The 8% truck mix used for the Airport Spur was obtained from Southeastern Wisconsin Regional Planning Commission (SEWRPC). This figure has since been increased to 9% to reflect the design addition of local street ramps at Howell Avenue.
SEWRPC's methods used in obtaining the truck mix are typical of these in highway planning and have been tested over the years and proven accurate within acceptable tolerance.
The character of I-94 is different than the Airport Spur. I-94 is a major highway between two major cities, Milwaukee and Chicago, while the Airport Spur will only carry traffic from Milwaukee and vicinity to the Airport.
